The repository cache is abstract-only. A separately archived full-text version supports the human XM_041725/770-residue COG7 construct, tagged HeLa localization and complex context. Bovine purification and Cog1/Cog2 mutant assays are distinct from COG7 experiments; historical sequence identity is not inferred from length alone.

Selected actual full Methods describe array-Y2H variants and validation subsets. One exact COG7–TAX1BP1 record includes the residue-749 variant feature and a no-effect classification. It is not silently converted to a featureless wild-type or independently validated pair.

The repository cache is abstract-only. Separately recovered original Methods, Table I and assembly Results describe human COG7 cDNA BE261220 in rabbit reticulocyte lysate and COG5/COG7 cooperation in assembly. Four exact target-paper interaction records cover COG4 and COG5. Possible endogenous lysate factors limit claims of purified binary directness.

Complete abstract and selected source context were read. Nine exact target-paper records cover MEOX2/Q6FHY5, TAX1BP1 and KIFC3-5, with current sequence reconstructions and all ROGIDs checked. Global isoform divergence does not establish an isoform-specific COG7 mechanism for each pair.

Genuine selected full text was read in patient/corrected-cell Methods/Results and Discussion. BFA redistribution, selective resident-protein localization and GS15 abundance are established. Failed rescue by tested degradation inhibitors limits the inferred stabilization mechanism; the original observations are retained.

Human knockout Results and Figure 3 document COG7-dependent lobe-B partner abundance, independently supporting complex maintenance. EM morphology and interface-assembly assays have distinct readouts. Toxin assays use representative knockout subsets; no uninspected COG7-specific toxin panel or glycosyltransferase catalysis is asserted.

Complete abstract and selected Introduction/Discussion were read; no separate target Methods claim is made. Four exact BioPlex records cover COG4 and COG5, two per partner across HEK293T/HCT116 contexts. AP-MS association does not establish a purified binary interface.

Actual Results/Discussion and assay-validation context were read. Six exact HuRI records cover TAX1BP1 and KIFC3-5. Screen-wide MAPPIT/GPCA validation is not attributed to these individual pairs; their exact Y2H records and product identities provide the target support.

The original publisher HTML was recovered and selected complete patient Results/Methods read. Two infants, patient fibroblasts and human COG7 complementation support a trafficking/glycosylation disorder. Assay differences between patients, residual COG7 and normal cathepsin-D transport are retained; detailed findings are not claimed to occur in the selected normal abstract.

Selected cache is marked full but its indexed body supplies Introduction and Discussion rather than target Methods/Results. Two complete exact anti-tag co-IP records authenticate human COG7 with mouse TRAF5/P70191 in a human host. The mixed-species association does not establish a COG7 immune-signaling function.

The repository cache is abstract-only. The separately recovered publisher-indexed original includes the COG7-knockdown Results, Figure 5 legend and selected RNAi/cell-culture Methods. It explicitly reports GM130/syntaxin-5 reduction in COG7 knockdown compared with mock or COG3 knockdown; the public source index supplies a literal excerpt, DOI and section locator. No full PDF or figure pixels were inspected. COG3 time courses, isolated vesicles and combined COG3/COG7 perturbations remain distinct; the stabilization mechanism is unresolved.

Genuine normal abstract explicitly reports Arabidopsis EYE/COG7 Golgi-size and protein-localization phenotypes. Complete current official donor records carry source-specific experimental premises. Original full Methods were not recovered; plant developmental roles are not added to human COG7.

Genuine full fly source was read for Cog7/GFP rescue, COG5 stability and Golgi morphology. Fly spermatogenesis and cytokinesis contexts are not assigned as new human functions. The current donor records are preserved separately from historical PAINT placement.

The full Methods/Results distinguish K. lactis structural fragments from human COG7 N-terminal interface tests. Human COG7 DDD mutation reduces recovered lobe-B assembly about twofold, rather than establishing a twofold decrease in total COG8 abundance. Glycosylation-rescue experiments test COG5 mutants, not a COG7 rescue construct.

Genuine selected full source supplies fly S2 Rab-affinity and mass-spectrometry context. The exact supplementary Cog7 target row was not inspected; the current donor IDA link is retained as literal database provenance, not claimed as independently verified target detection.

ontology.label: protein-macromolecule adaptor activity
ontology.definition: An adaptor activity that brings together two or more macromolecules in contact, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way. The adaptor can bring together two proteins, or a protein and another macromolecule such as a lipid or a nucleic acid.

ontology.label: enzyme binding
ontology.definition: Binding to an enzyme, a protein with catalytic activity.

ontology.label: Golgi apparatus
ontology.definition: A membrane-bound cytoplasmic organelle of the endomembrane system that further processes the core oligosaccharides (e.g. N-glycans) added to proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum and packages them into membrane-bound vesicles. The Golgi apparatus operates at the intersection of the secretory, lysosomal, and endocytic pathways.

ontology.label: protein binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a protein.

ontology.label: COG complex
ontology.definition: A multisubunit tethering complex of the CATCHR family (complexes associated with tethering containing helical rods) that has a role in tethering vesicles to the Golgi prior to fusion. Composed of 8 subunits COG1-8.

ontology.label: protein domain specific binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a specific domain of a protein.

ontology.label: helical-bundle zippering fusogenic activity
ontology.definition: Acting as a marker to identify a membrane and interacting selectively with one or more SNAREs on another membrane to mediate membrane fusion.

ontology.label: intracellular protein transport
ontology.definition: The directed movement of proteins in a cell, including the movement of proteins between specific compartments or structures within a cell, such as organelles of a eukaryotic cell.

ontology.label: retrograde vesicle-mediated transport, Golgi to endoplasmic reticulum
ontology.definition: The directed movement of substances from the Golgi back to the endoplasmic reticulum, mediated by vesicles bearing specific protein coats such as COPI or COG.

ontology.label: Golgi membrane
ontology.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments of the Golgi apparatus.

ontology.label: protein localization to organelle
ontology.definition: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a location within an organelle.

ontology.label: protein retention in Golgi apparatus
ontology.definition: The retention of proteins within the Golgi apparatus. Golgi-localized carbohydrate-modifying enzymes have a short N-terminal domain that faces the cytosol, a single transmembrane alpha helix, and a large C-terminal domain that faces the Golgi lumen and that contains the catalytic site. How the membrane-spanning alpha helix in a Golgi enzyme causes its localization and prevents its movement to the plasma membrane is not known.

ontology.label: protein stabilization
ontology.definition: Any process involved in maintaining the structure and integrity of a protein and preventing it from degradation or aggregation.

ontology.label: protein localization to Golgi apparatus
ontology.definition: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a location within the Golgi apparatus.

ontology.label: retrograde transport, vesicle recycling within Golgi
ontology.definition: The retrograde movement of substances within the Golgi, mediated by COP I vesicles. Cis-Golgi vesicles are constantly moving forward through the Golgi stack by cisternal progression, eventually becoming trans-Golgi vesicles. They then selectively transport membrane and luminal proteins from the trans- to the medial-Golgi while leaving others behind in the trans-Golgi cisternae; similarly, they selectively move proteins from the medial- to the cis-Golgi.

ontology.label: glycoprotein biosynthetic process
ontology.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glycoproteins, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

ontology.label: Golgi organization
ontology.definition: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the Golgi apparatus.

ontology.label: protein complex scaffold activity
ontology.definition: A structural molecule activity of a protein-containing complex component that serves to hold the complex together. Protein complex scaffolds are integral members of complexes.

ontology.label: trans-Golgi network membrane
ontology.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments that make up the trans-Golgi network.

ontology.label: kinesin binding
ontology.definition: Interacting selectively and non-covalently and stoichiometrically with kinesin, a member of a superfamily of microtubule-based motor proteins that perform force-generating tasks such as organelle transport and chromosome segregation.

ontology.label: ATPase binding
ontology.definition: Binding to an ATPase, any enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of ATP.

ontology.label: DNA-binding transcription factor binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a DNA-binding transcription factor, a protein that interacts with a specific DNA sequence (sometimes referred to as a motif) within the regulatory region of a gene to modulate transcription.

current_term_definitions.label: obsolete cargo receptor ligand activity

current_term_definitions.label: protein complex scaffold activity

current_term_definitions.label: DNA-binding transcription factor binding

current_term_definitions.label: bHLH transcription factor binding
current_term_definitions.definition: Binding to a basic Helix-Loop-Helix (bHLH) superfamily of transcription factors, important regulatory components in transcriptional networks of many developmental pathways.

current_term_definitions.label: cAMP response element binding protein binding
current_term_definitions.definition: Binding to a cAMP response element binding protein (a CREB protein).

current_term_definitions.label: RNA polymerase II-specific DNA-binding transcription factor binding
current_term_definitions.definition: Binding to a sequence-specific DNA binding RNA polymerase II transcription factor, any of the factors that interact selectively and non-covalently with a specific DNA sequence in order to modulate transcription.

current_term_definitions.label: nuclear receptor binding
current_term_definitions.definition: Binding to a nuclear receptor protein. Nuclear receptor proteins are DNA-binding transcription factors which are regulated by binding to a ligand.

current_term_definitions.label: Tat protein binding
current_term_definitions.definition: Binding to Tat, a viral transactivating regulatory protein from the human immunodeficiency virus, or the equivalent protein from another virus.

current_term_definitions.label: NF-kappaB binding
current_term_definitions.definition: Binding to NF-kappaB, a transcription factor for eukaryotic RNA polymerase II promoters.

current_term_definitions.label: NFAT protein binding
current_term_definitions.definition: Binding to NFAT (nuclear factor of activated T cells) proteins, a family of transcription factors. NFAT proteins have crucial roles in the development and function of the immune system.

current_term_definitions.label: STAT family protein binding
current_term_definitions.definition: Binding to a member of the signal transducers and activators of transcription (STAT) protein family. STATs are, as the name indicates, both signal transducers and transcription factors. STATs are activated by cytokines and some growth factors and thus control important biological processes including cell growth, cell differentiation, apoptosis and immune responses.

followup_4912.binding_records_scope: The existing full literal records remain unchanged. Array, pooling and validated-two-hybrid labels are pipeline stages; records and overlapping screen publications are not counted as independent biological replications. Natural colocalization and exact-product activity were not established by these pairs.

changed_reviews.summary: COG7 provides a structural interface for lobe-B assembly.
changed_reviews.reason: The original human reconstruction shows cooperative incorporation of COG6 by COG5 plus COG7 and optimal COG8 incorporation with the lobe-B partners. Independent human COG7 interface mutations impair COG5 association and reduce recovered lobe-B assembly. Together these establish performed structural assembly, supporting protein complex scaffold activity. The crystallographic fragments are from K. lactis, and the glycosylation-rescue experiment tests COG5 mutants; neither is presented as a full-length human COG7 assay. Human COG7 knockout also reduces the abundance of its lobe-B partners; this supports complex maintenance, separately from the measured interface and assembly assays.

The HI-II-14 supplies three positive TAX1BP1–COG7 records labelled array, pooling and validated two hybrid. These records describe stages of a shared Y2H screening pipeline, not independent biological replications. TAX1BP1 is an experimentally supported ubiquitin-binding adaptor and selective-autophagy receptor. Those activities characterize the partner but do not identify a more specific applicable binding class here: binding an adaptor is not itself adaptor activity, and this pair does not establish ligand-triggered cargo-receptor activity. The positive generic interaction is retained without requiring a mapped interface or native colocalization.

changed_reviews.summary: Refine the MEOX2 interaction to RNA polymerase II-specific transcription-factor binding.
changed_reviews.reason: The three positive Q6FHY5 records identify array, pooling and validated-two-hybrid stages of one screen, not three independent replications. The exact 303-residue product differs from reviewed P50222 by one glutamine outside its unchanged homeobox. P50222 has experimentally supported RNA polymerase II-specific transcription-activator and sequence-specific DNA-binding functions. This supports the more specific partner class, with an explicit reference-product inference; the screen does not itself assay Q6FHY5 transcriptional activity. Neither compartment differences nor paper count negate the recorded binding, and no COG7 transcriptional role or native nuclear interaction is inferred.

changed_reviews.summary: COG7 supports maintenance of selected Golgi proteins.
changed_reviews.reason: The original human HeLa COG7-knockdown Results and Figure 5 legend explicitly compare mock, COG3 and COG7 depletion: GM130 and syntaxin-5 abundance decrease in COG7-knockdown cells, and the short Golgi syntaxin-5 form is particularly affected. These are COG7 observations, not transferred COG3 results. The short literal excerpt and original DOI/section locator are provided in the source-evidence index because the publication cache contains only the abstract. This supports complex-mediated maintenance under the broad protein-stabilization definition, integrated with the scaffold core. It identifies neither direct protective contact nor a degradation pathway. Greater GlcNAcT1 instability after combined COG3/COG7 depletion remains a combined-perturbation result.

changed_reviews.summary: COG7 supports cellular maintenance of GS15.
changed_reviews.reason: COG7-deficient patient fibroblasts lose GS15 abundance and normal localization, both restored by COG7 correction. This supports complex-mediated protein maintenance within the scaffold core. The broad protein-stabilization process does not require isolated chaperone chemistry. Tested proteasomal and lysosomal inhibitors fail to restore GS15, leaving the depletion mechanism unresolved rather than contradicting maintenance. Variable changes in other residents are not generalized as uniformly COG7 dependent.
